# Contributing to Go

Go is an open source project.

It is the work of hundreds of contributors. We appreciate your help!

## Before filing an issue

If you are unsure whether you have found a bug, please consider asking in the [golang-nuts mailing
list](https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/golang-nuts) or [other forums](https://golang.org/help/) first. If
the behavior you are seeing is confirmed as a bug or issue, it can easily be re-raised in the issue tracker.

## Filing issues

Sensitive security-related issues should be reported to [security@golang.org](mailto:security@golang.org).
See the [security policy](https://golang.org/security) for details.

The recommended way to file an issue is by running `go bug`.
Otherwise, when filing an issue, make sure to answer these five questions:

1. What version of Go are you using (`go version`)?
2. What operating system and processor architecture are you using?
3. What did you do?
4. What did you expect to see?
5. What did you see instead?

For change proposals, see [Proposing Changes To Go](https://go.dev/s/proposal-process).

## Contributing code

Please read the [Contribution Guidelines](https://golang.org/doc/contribute.html) before sending patches.

Unless otherwise noted, the Go source files are distributed under
the BSD-style license found in the LICENSE file.

# The Go Programming Language

Go is an open source programming language that makes it easy to build simple,
reliable, and efficient software.

![Gopher image](https://golang.org/doc/gopher/fiveyears.jpg)
*Gopher image by [Renee French][rf], licensed under [Creative Commons 4.0 Attribution license][cc4-by].*

Our canonical Git repository is located at https://go.googlesource.com/go.
There is a mirror of the repository at https://github.com/golang/go.

Unless otherwise noted, the Go source files are distributed under the
BSD-style license found in the LICENSE file.

### Download and Install

#### Binary Distributions

Official binary distributions are available at https://go.dev/dl/.

After downloading a binary release, visit https://go.dev/doc/install
for installation instructions.

#### Install From Source

If a binary distribution is not available for your combination of
operating system and architecture, visit
https://go.dev/doc/install/source
for source installation instructions.

### Contributing

Go is the work of thousands of contributors. We appreciate your help!

To contribute, please read the contribution guidelines at https://go.dev/doc/contribute.

Note that the Go project uses the issue tracker for bug reports and
proposals only. See https://go.dev/wiki/Questions for a list of
places to ask questions about the Go language.

[rf]: https://reneefrench.blogspot.com/
[cc4-by]: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

report.overview: This is the golang/go repository — the complete source of the Go programming language toolchain. It contains the standard library and runtime under src/, the cmd/ suite of tools (go command, compiler, linker, assembler, cgo, vet, gofmt, pprof, trace, and the cmd/dist bootstrap/test orchestrator), a ~2000-file black-box regression corpus under test/, frozen public-API manifests under api/, and per-release notes under doc/. The system is self-hosting: building requires an existing Go toolchain (GOROOT_BOOTSTRAP >= Go 1.26.0), which first compiles cmd/dist, and dist then bootstraps toolchain1 (asm/cgo/compile/link) and a go_bootstrap binary that rebuilds everything else.

system_map.summary: The repo is the entire Go distribution: src/ holds the standard library (module 'std'), the runtime, and all toolchain commands under src/cmd/ (module 'cmd'). The build is bootstrapped: src/make.bash compiles src/cmd/dist with a pre-existing Go (GOROOT_BOOTSTRAP), then 'dist bootstrap' builds the compiler/linker/asm and a go_bootstrap binary which rebuilds the full tree. The go command (src/cmd/go) is the user-facing front end dispatching to ~20 subcommands; compilation flows through cmd/compile (frontend+SSA backend) and cmd/link. Tests are orchestrated by 'go tool dist test' (src/cmd/dist/test.go) plus the cmd/internal/testdir harness for the test/ corpus. API stability is enforced by golden manifests in api/ checked by src/cmd/api tests.

claims.claim: The repo is the Go toolchain itself: src/ contains the stdlib (module 'std', go 1.28) with vendored deps golang.org/x/crypto, x/net, x/sys, x/text; cmd/ is a separate module 'cmd' with its own vendor tree.
Building from source runs src/make.bash from $GOROOT/src, which locates GOROOT_BOOTSTRAP (a Go tree >= 1.26.0, bootgo=1.26.0), builds ./cmd/dist with it, then executes './cmd/dist/dist bootstrap -a'.

cmd/dist's cmdbootstrap() pins GOPATH to $GOROOT/pkg/obj/gopath, sets GOPROXY=off and GOCACHE=$GOROOT/pkg/obj/go-build, forces GOEXPERIMENT=none for toolchain1, then calls bootstrapBuildTools() to build cmd/asm, cmd/cgo, cmd/compile, cmd/link, cmd/preprofile and go_bootstrap.
make.bash refuses to run on Windows (use make.bat), rejects gold linker 2.20, warns about SELinux execstack policy, and forbids GOROOT_BOOTSTRAP == GOROOT.

The go command entrypoint src/cmd/go/main.go registers all subcommands into base.Go.Commands in init(), then in main() runs telemetry setup, handleChdirFlag, toolchain.Select, flag parsing, lookupCmd, and invoke(cmd, args).
base.Command is the universal command abstraction: fields Run, UsageLine, Short, Long, Flag, CustomFlags, Commands; Runnable() is Run != nil; help topics are non-runnable Commands.

The compiler binary cmd/compile/main.go selects a per-architecture initializer from the archInits map (386, amd64, arm, arm64, loong64, mips*, ppc64*, riscv64, s390x, wasm) keyed on buildcfg.GOARCH, then calls gc.Main(archInit).

The linker cmd/link/internal/ld parses a large flag surface (-o, -buildid, -race/-msan/-asan, -linkmode via extld, -checklinkname, -randlayout, -k field tracking) and supports internal linking or delegation to an external linker.

The runtime scheduler in src/runtime/proc.go implements the G/M/P model (goroutines, OS threads, processors) with distributed per-P run queues, a global run queue, spinning-thread protocol (m.spinning, sched.nmspinning) and work stealing in findRunnable.

The GC in src/runtime/mgc.go is a concurrent, non-generational, non-compacting mark-and-sweep with a hybrid write barrier, per-P size-segregated allocation, and a GC rate governed by GOGC (default 100).
Build configuration is centralized in internal/buildcfg: GOARCH/GOOS plus micro-arch levels GOAMD64/GOARM64/GORISCV64 etc., GO_LDSO, GOFIPS140, and buildcfg.Check() exits tools on invalid values.
go.env at repo root seeds defaults GOPROXY=https://proxy.golang.org,direct, GOSUMDB=sum.golang.org, GOTOOLCHAIN=auto — the checksum DB and auto toolchain download are on by default.

Test execution is orchestrated by cmd/dist's 'dist test' subcommand (tester struct with race/msan/asan/compile-only modes, -run regexp, JSON output), invoked by run.bash as '../bin/go tool dist test -rebuild'.

api/ contains frozen per-release API manifests (go1.txt..go1.27.txt, except.txt) plus a mutable api/next; src/cmd/api tests walk the stdlib API and compare against these files to enforce Go 1 compatibility.

feature_catalog.summary: User-facing surface is dominated by the 'go' command: build/install/run/test/list/doc/env/clean/fmt/fix/generate/get/mod/vet/version/work/tool/telemetry/bug plus ~18 help topics. Inside that, the big subsystems are the module system (modload/modfetch/mvs/vcs), the parallel action-graph build engine with content-hash caching (work.Builder), cgo/SWIG foreign-function builds, coverage instrumentation, PGO, FIPS-140 crypto mode, toolchain auto-switching, and opt-in telemetry. Separate binaries ship gofmt, vet, pprof, trace, cover, covdata, test2json, asm, link, compile, cgo, nm, objdump, pack, addr2line, buildid, dist, distpack, preprofile, relnote.

claims.claim: go subcommands registered in main.go init(): bug, build, clean, doc, env, fix, fmt, generate, get, install, list, mod, run, telemetry, test, tool, version, vet, work — plus help topics (buildconstraint, buildjson, buildmode, c, cache, environment, filetype, goauth, gopath, goproxy, importpath, module-auth, modules, packages, private, testflag, testfunc, vcs).
'go mod' has subcommands download, edit, graph, init, tidy, vendor, verify, why (one file each under cmd/go/internal/modcmd); 'go work' has edit, init, sync, use, vendor.

GOTOOLCHAIN auto-switching: toolchain.Select() runs early in main, reads go.mod/go.work toolchain lines, downloads golang.org/toolchain v0.0.1-<version>.<goos>-<goarch> modules and re-execs the target binary, bounded by maxSwitch=100 loop detection via GOTOOLCHAIN_INTERNAL_SWITCH_COUNT.
The build engine work.Builder.Do executes a depth-first-prioritized action DAG with content-hash caching (buildActionID via sha256), trimming the default build cache on completion.

cgo support: exec.go contains runCgo, processCgoOutputs, dynimport, swig/swigOne/swigVersionCheck, and C compiler invocation helpers (gcc, gxx, gfortran, gccld, PkgconfigCmd) honoring CGO flags and pkg-config.
Coverage: runCover/cover/writeCoverPkgInputs instrument packages during 'go test -cover'/'go build -cover', producing covmeta files consumed by cmd/cover and cmd/covdata.
Vet is wired into 'go test': buildVetConfig/vet actions run analysis passes (golang.org/x/tools/go/analysis) as part of the test action graph.
PGO: compiler flag -pgo loads a profile via pgoir.New in gc.Main, feeding weighted call graphs into interleaved.DevirtualizeAndInlinePackage.

FIPS 140 support: GOFIPS140 env var validated in buildcfg (off/latest/inprocess/certified/v1.Y.Z), fips140 package in cmd/go, crypto implementation under src/crypto/internal/fips140 with GOFIPS140 zip shipping in the distribution.

Telemetry: opt-in counters via cmd/internal/telemetry/counter (counter.Open, counter.Inc, CountFlags) throughout main.go and the compiler, managed by 'go telemetry' and a sidecar child/parent upload model (telemetry.MaybeChild/MaybeParent).
'go generate' scans //go:generate directives; test flag defs are generated: cmd/go/internal/test/genflags.go generates flagdefs.go shared between go test and vet.

Standalone tools shipped under src/cmd: asm, cgo, compile, link, gofmt, vet, pprof, trace, cover, covdata, test2json, nm, objdump, pack, addr2line, buildid, fix, api, dist, distpack, export, preprofile, relnote.

The stdlib itself is a feature surface of ~150 packages under src/ including net/http, crypto/tls, os/exec, plugin, embed, testing, runtime/trace, and newer ones like simd, weak, unique, arena, structs, uuid.
Runtime GODEBUG compatibility settings are user-facing knobs documented in doc/godebug.md and registered in internal/godebugs/table.go; removed settings cause a fatal at startup.

data_flow.summary: End-to-end: user args → cmd/go/main → toolchain.Select (may re-exec a downloaded toolchain) → load.Package resolution via go.mod/go.work → modload computes the build list with MVS, fetching modules through modfetch (GOPROXY → zip → sumdb/go.sum verify → modcache) or vcs direct → work.Builder builds an action DAG (compile/cgo/cover/vet/link actions) keyed by sha256 action IDs against the build cache → cmd/compile turns source through noder/typecheck/inline/escape/walk into SSA and object files → cmd/link consumes objects+importcfg and emits the binary. At runtime, compiled binaries start in runtime.main which enables GC and runs init tasks before main.main.

claims.claim: Package loading produces load.Package structs; PackagePublic fields are declared part of the go command's public API for 'go list -json' and must stay in sync with list.go.
Module graph resolution: modload.Init loads go.mod/go.work, LoadPackages resolves import patterns to modules; the toolchain module itself is special-cased (ErrToolchain on Download).

Module fetch path: Fetcher.Download → downloadCache.Do (dedup) → download → checkMod verifies against go.sum and the checksum database → unzip into GOMODCACHE; a TooNewError is raised if the module's go directive exceeds the local toolchain.

Non-proxy resolution goes through cmd/go/internal/vcs: vcsList = [hg, git, svn, fossil], each a Cmd describing binary name, schemes, root-detection; IsSecure gates insecure schemes (https/git+ssh/svn+ssh/ssh allowed; GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL overrides for git).

Build action graph: Builder.Do assigns DFS post-order priorities, each action's cache key is buildActionID hashing inputs/flags/toolchain IDs; cache hits short-circuit compile steps; cgo, cover, vet, link are distinct action types.

Compiler pipeline in gc.Main: noder.LoadPackage (parse+typecheck via types2 machinery) → bloop markings → interleaved.DevirtualizeAndInlinePackage (with optional PGO profile) → loopvar capture fixes → pkginit.MakeTask → escape.Funcs → rewriteresults/slice transforms → enqueueFunc→compileFunctions→SSA backend → dumpobj writes the object file.
The SSA backend pass list is a static ordered table `passes` in ssacompile/compile.go run by ssa.Compile; phases are checked for ordering violations and support per-pass debug flags via -d=ssa/...

Link flow: Builder.link writes an importcfg (writeLinkImportcfg), invokes cmd/link which loads goobj objects via cmd/internal/goobj, performs deadcode elimination/address layout, and stamps a buildid; external link mode delegates to extld.

Runtime startup data flow: runtime.main (on g0/m0) → doInit(runtime_inittasks) → gcenable() → doInit over each moduledata's inittasks (linker-computed init graph) → close(mainInitDoneChan) → main_main() i.e. user's main.

Goroutine lifecycle: newproc/newproc1 creates a g, runqput places it on a P run queue or runnext, wakep may unpark an M; schedule→findRunnable→execute→gogo runs it; timers and netpoll feed the same queues.

GC cycle data flow: sweep termination STW → concurrent mark with write barrier shading and mutator assists → distributed termination detection (gcMarkDone) → mark termination STW → concurrent sweep; heap goal driven by GOGC.
go test data flow: runTest → builderTest constructs buildAction/runAction/printAction triples; a generated testmain binary runs and its output is piped through test2json for -json reporting.
Telemetry data flow: counters are written to a counter file opened at startup (skipped for 'go telemetry off'); MaybeParent spawns the upload sidecar; CountFlags records flag usage patterns.

API check data flow: cmd/api tests walk each stdlib package's exported API via go/ast and compare against golden lines in api/go1*.txt + api/next, with per-feature proposal issue annotations required since go1.19.

behavior_traces.summary: Four flows were walked end-to-end. (1) Source bootstrap: make.bash → dist → bootstrapBuildTools → go_bootstrap rebuild. (2) 'go build': main → toolchain.Select → lookupCmd → invoke → load → Builder.Do. (3) Module fetch with integrity checks. (4) Runtime program startup and the scheduler loop. Test orchestration via run.bash → dist test → testdir is a fifth traced path.

claims.claim: BOOTSTRAP trace: src/make.bash → check env (Windows, gold ld, SELinux) → locate GOROOT_BOOTSTRAP → 'go build -o cmd/dist/dist ./cmd/dist' → 'dist env -p' → 'dist bootstrap -a' → cmdbootstrap() → setup()+writeGeneratedFiles() → checkCC()+bootstrapBuildTools() → go_bootstrap rebuilds std+cmd; the dist binary is deleted afterward.

'go build' trace: main() → telemetry.MaybeChild/counter.Open → handleChdirFlag (-C must be first) → toolchain.Select (may download+re-exec newer toolchain) → flag.Parse → lookupCmd(args) → invoke() → buildcfg.Check → envcmd.MkEnv applied → cmd.Run → runBuild → load.PackagesAndTests → Builder.Do(root).

Compile action trace: Builder.buildObject → resolve inputs → (cgo path: runCgo→processCgoOutputs→ccompile/dynimport) → run 'compile' tool with importcfg → cacheObjdirFile stores outputs under the action ID → link action writes final binary.

Module download trace: Fetcher.Download → checkCacheDir → downloadCache.Do → DownloadDir probe → download (proxy via GOPROXY or VCS fallback) → checkMod (go.sum + sumdb/dirhash verification) → TooNewError check on module's go directive → extracted dir under GOMODCACHE.

Runtime startup trace: rt0/schedinit (asm + runtime1) → mstart/mstart0/mstart1 → runtime.main on main goroutine: set maxstacksize (1GB/64-bit) → newm(sysmon) → lockOSThread → nanotime → doInit(runtime_inittasks) → gcenable → defaultGOMAXPROCSUpdateEnable → cgo init checks (_cgo_notify_runtime_init_done, startTemplateThread) → doInit per-module inittasks → unlockOSThread → call main_main (user main) → exit.

Scheduler loop trace: goready/newproc → runqput (local runnext/runq or global) → wakep if spinning==0 and idle P → M spins in findRunnable (local queue → global → netpoll → steal from other P) → schedule() resets spinning, handles lockedm via startlockedm → execute(gp, inheritTime) → gogo jumps to goroutine.

GC trigger trace: allocation or force → gcStart → sweep termination STW → gcphase=_GCmark + write barrier enable → start world, mark workers + assists drain grey queue → gcMarkDone distributed termination → mark termination STW → _GCoff, concurrent sweep resumes.

Test-dir trace: run.bash → 'go tool dist test -rebuild' → tester.run enumerates distTests → for test/ corpus: 'go test cmd/internal/testdir' → Test() reads 'go env -json', iterates dirs=[.,ken,chan,interface,...,codegen,fixedbugs,...], registers each .go file as subtest Test/<rel path> honoring //-directives (run, errorcheck, compile).

Toolchain switch trace: Select → modload.NewLoader().WillBeEnabled → read go.mod 'toolchain' line → compare with local version → if newer needed: modfetch downloads golang.org/toolchain@v0.0.1-<ver>.<os>-<arch> → exec new go binary with GOTOOLCHAIN_INTERNAL_SWITCH_VERSION set → child verifies and clears it; maxSwitch=100 aborts loops.

cgo trace: package with import "C" → runCgo generates _cgo_gotypes.go etc → processCgoOutputs compiles generated C via gcc (ccompile with DefaultCFlags='-O2 -g') → dynimport produces dynamic symbols → swig path handles .swig/.swigcxx files → objects linked into the package.

testing_signals.summary: Testing is massive and layered: package-level Go tests throughout stdlib and cmd, the ~1900-file test/ black-box corpus driven by cmd/internal/testdir with //-directive comments, cmd/go's script-based tests under testdata/script using the cmd/internal/script engine, dist-level orchestration with race/msan/asan/compile-only modes, and API golden tests. CI is not GitHub Actions — .github contains only templates; testing runs on Go's own builder fleet via all.bash/run.bash with sharding support.

claims.claim: testdir_test.go runs every test/*.go file as a subtest 'Test/<path>' over dirs {., ken, chan, interface, internal/runtime/sys, syntax, dwarf, fixedbugs, codegen, abi, typeparam, arenas, simd}; directives like '// run' and '// errorcheck' in each file control execution; flags -shard/-shards/-target/-update_errors/-all_codegen exist.

run.bash exports GOENV=off, GOPATH=/nonexist-gopath, disables core dumps, then execs 'go tool dist test -rebuild'; GO_TEST_SHARDS (default 1, or 10 on builders), GO_BUILDER_NAME, GO_TEST_SHORT, GO_TEST_TIMEOUT_SCALE control behavior.

cmd/dist/test.go's tester supports -race, -msan, -asan, -compile-only, -k (keep going), -run regexp (invertible with '!'), -json output; tests are grouped under headings and run as parallel work items.
cmd/go has extensive tests: go_test.go, plus script-driven tests in src/cmd/go/testdata/script executed by the cmd/internal/script engine (engine.go, conds.go, cmds_*.go).
API compatibility is tested by src/cmd/api: api_test.go TestGolden/TestCompareAPI walks exported symbols and diffs against api/go1*.txt + api/next; boring_test.go covers FIPS API differences.

The compiler backend is heavily unit-tested in-tree: ssacompile has ~30 *_test.go files (prove_test, fuse_test, rewriteCond_test, looprotate_test, regalloc_test, schedule_test, etc.); test/codegen files assert generated-assembly patterns.
cmd/go/internal/verylongtest exists as a separate package for tests too slow for normal runs; run.bash's GO_TEST_SHORT plumbing distinguishes short vs long builders.
internal/testenv provides test helpers (GoToolPath, Builder) used by testdir and other cmd tests to locate the freshly built toolchain and detect builder environment.
buildall.bash/race.bash/clean.bash in src/ provide cross-compile and race-mode build verification; all.bash chains make.bash + run.bash + 'dist banner'.

There are no GitHub Actions workflows: .github/ contains only CODE_OF_CONDUCT, ISSUE_TEMPLATE, PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE, SUPPORT; review runs on Gerrit (codereview.cfg) with LUCI builders — CI config is external to the repo (x/build).
VCS behavior is tested hermetically: cmd/go/internal/vcweb.Server hosts fake repos (VCSTestRepoURL/VCSTestHosts/VCSTestIsLocalHost hooks in vcs.go) so tests don't hit the network.
Test flag definitions are shared and generated: genflags.go emits flagdefs.go so 'go test' flags and vet/test2json stay consistent; flagdefs_test.go verifies.

risk_map.summary: Highest-risk surfaces: (1) supply-chain code execution — toolchain auto-download+re-exec, module fetches, VCS shell-outs, and cgo/gcc/swig invocation; (2) runtime invariants where a single mistake corrupts all programs (scheduler throws, GC write barriers, linkname/unsafe); (3) bootstrap trust — the build requires a pre-existing Go binary; (4) compatibility enforcement — api/ files and GODEBUG semantics are contractual. Many security gates exist (sumdb verification, IsSecure scheme checks, #cgo flag validation) but bypass knobs (GOINSECURE, GONOSUMDB/GONOSUMCHECK, GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL, -insecure) weaken them.

claims.claim: toolchain.Select can download and exec a different toolchain binary on every invocation; the internal switch protocol (targetEnv/countEnv) is filtered from user env via FilterEnv, but a compromised proxy/toolchain module would execute arbitrary code — mitigated by sumdb verification and maxSwitch loop detection.

modfetch unzips remotely fetched archives into the module cache; integrity depends on checkMod comparing against go.sum and sum.golang.org (dirhash); Fetcher.Unzip bypass path exists for shipped GOFIPS140 zips.

vcs.go executes git/hg/svn/fossil binaries against module-controlled repo URLs; scheme security is enforced via isSecureScheme (https/ssh only) and honors GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL, but repo-root discovery parses remote HTML/meta tags via cmd/go/internal/web.

cgo compiles package-supplied C/C++/Fortran and runs pkg-config and swig; buildFlags validates #cgo flags (security against flag injection), DefaultCFlags='-O2 -g'; malicious module C sources execute at build time.

The scheduler has many hard invariants enforced by throw() — 'schedule: holding locks', 'schedule: in cgo', 'runtime.main not on m0', 'nanotime returning zero' — a violation crashes the whole program; the spinning-thread protocol comment documents known underutilization race windows.

GC correctness depends on write-barrier discipline; the compiler's nowritebarrierrec check (ssagen.EnableNoWriteBarrierRecCheck/NoWriteBarrierRecCheck) runs only when compiling the runtime — a fragile coupling between compiler flags and runtime safety.

Bootstrap requires trusting a prebuilt Go >= 1.26.0 (GOROOT_BOOTSTRAP); make.bash refuses GOROOT_BOOTSTRAP==GOROOT but cannot verify provenance — classic trusting-trust exposure; GOEXPERIMENT is deliberately forced to 'none' for toolchain1 to avoid skew.

make.bash contains environment probes that can block or corrupt builds: gold 2.20 ld detection, SELinux allow_execstack check, src/pkg staleness fatal in cmdbootstrap — build failures here are environment-specific and hard to reproduce.

//go:linkname and unsafe let user code bypass type safety into runtime internals; linker flag -checklinkname (default true) exists specifically to police linkname references, indicating a known abuse vector; test/linkname.dir exercises it.

Telemetry writes counter files and spawns upload sidecars (MaybeChild/MaybeParent) — privacy-sensitive surface; special-cased so 'go telemetry off' works without opening counter files, and cmdIsGoTelemetryOff scans os.Args pre-parse.
Removed GODEBUG settings produce a fatal() at program startup — a deliberate compat break that can kill binaries built with older defaults if the env carries stale settings.

api/ files are a contractual freeze: adding to a released go1.N.txt is forbidden (files 'add new lines but do not remove any'), and post-1.19 entries must cite a proposal issue — editing the wrong file silently breaks the compatibility checker.
Two parallel type checkers exist (go/types in std and cmd/compile/internal/types2 for the compiler) that must be kept in sync; skew between them is a recurring correctness risk.

Generated files must stay in sync with generators: flagdefs.go (from genflags.go), opGen.go/rewrite rules in ssacompile, and files produced by writeGeneratedFiles in dist; editing outputs without regenerating causes subtle drift.

extension_points.summary: Extension is table-driven almost everywhere: new 'go' subcommands register in main.go's command table; new architectures add an Init func to cmd/compile's archInits map plus an ssagen.ArchInfo; new SSA passes go in the ordered passes table; new VCS tools extend vcsList; experiments are file-pairs in internal/goexperiment; GODEBUGs register in internal/godebugs/table.go; new stdlib API must add lines to api/next and release notes under doc/next; new test/ cases just drop files into the enumerated dirs.

claims.claim: New 'go' subcommands: create a package under cmd/go/internal/<name>, define a &base.Command{Run, UsageLine, Flag, ...}, and append it to base.Go.Commands in cmd/go/main.go init().
Nested subcommand groups work via Command.Commands (e.g. 'go mod', 'go work'); Lookup ignores non-runnable entries so help topics coexist in the same table.

New CPU architecture: add an entry to archInits in cmd/compile/main.go mapping GOARCH name to an Init(*ssagen.ArchInfo), implement the arch package under cmd/compile/internal/<arch>, and add a linker backend dir under cmd/link/internal/<arch>.

New SSA optimization pass: append to the `passes` table in ssacompile/compile.go (line ~414); ordering is verified ('passes %s and %s out of order') and each pass gets timing/debug plumbing automatically.
New VCS support: add a *Cmd to vcsList in vcs.go with Name/Cmd/Env/Roots/Scheme/PingCmd/Status; secure schemes come from defaultSecureScheme.

New toolchain experiment: add exp_<name>_on.go/exp_<name>_off.go file pairs in src/internal/goexperiment (existing pairs: arenas, boringcrypto, cgocheck2, dwarf5, fieldtrack, ...); buildcfg surfaces them via GOEXPERIMENT.
New GODEBUG compatibility setting: register in internal/godebugs/table.go, document in doc/godebug.md; runtime reads values and fatals on removed ones.
New stdlib API: implementation in src/<pkg>, one line in api/next/*.txt with proposal issue annotation, release-note entry under doc/next/6-stdlib; the api test enforces the manifest.
New regression test: drop a .go file with a '// run'/'// errorcheck' comment into test/ or test/fixedbugs; it is picked up automatically by testdir without registration.
New cmd/go script test: add a txtar script under src/cmd/go/testdata/script; the cmd/internal/script engine interprets commands/conditions without code changes.
New telemetry counter: call counter.New("name") / counter.Inc in cmd or compiler code; CountFlags auto-instruments flag usage per subcommand.
Build-time microarch targeting is env-extensible: GOAMD64/GOARM64/GORISCV64 etc. parsed in buildcfg; adding a level means extending the envOr validators, not the tools.
Vet analysis passes plug in through golang.org/x/tools/go/analysis (imported by work/exec.go), so new analyzers come from the x/tools module rather than this repo.

agent_handoff.summary: Working rules: never build inside a pristine checkout without a bootstrap Go; run tests via the built tree's ../bin/go, not a system go. The safe edit boundary is: stdlib packages are ordinary Go code, but runtime, compiler SSA tables, api/ manifests, and cmd/go internals have hard invariants and generated files. Always read the file's package comment first — cmd/dist, runtime/proc.go, mgc.go and gc/main.go carry long design comments that encode the actual contract. After edits, run the package's own tests plus cmd/internal/testdir for anything touching the toolchain.

claims.claim: Build: 'cd src && ./make.bash' (needs GOROOT_BOOTSTRAP >= Go 1.26.0); full validation: ./all.bash which runs make.bash + run.bash; test-only: 'cd src && ./run.bash' or '../bin/go test cmd/internal/testdir -run=Test/<file>'.

Read first for any toolchain change: src/cmd/go/main.go (command wiring), src/cmd/go/internal/base/base.go (Command contract), src/cmd/go/internal/work/exec.go (build engine), src/cmd/go/internal/load/pkg.go (Package model), src/cmd/go/internal/modload/init.go (module state).

Read first for compiler work: src/cmd/compile/main.go, src/cmd/compile/internal/gc/main.go (the phase ordering is the file), src/cmd/compile/internal/ssacompile/compile.go (pass table); for runtime work: src/runtime/proc.go and src/runtime/mgc.go headers are mandatory.
make.bash explicitly forbids new code after the bootstrap call — additions belong in cmd/dist's cmdbootstrap so all three shell variants (make.bash/make.bat/make.rc) stay minimal.
api/go1*.txt files are frozen once shipped; only api/next/* is mutable and each new line needs a '#nnnnn' proposal issue annotation; except.txt lists permitted exceptions.

PackagePublic in load/pkg.go is a public API surface ('okay to add fields, but not to change or remove existing ones. Keep in sync with ../list/list.go') — renaming a field breaks 'go list -json' consumers.

Generated-code traps: cmd/go/internal/test/flagdefs.go is produced by genflags.go; ssacompile/opGen.go and rewrite tables are generated; dist's writeGeneratedFiles produces version/config files — regenerate rather than hand-editing.

Error conventions: go-command code uses base.Fatalf/base.Errorf (exit status via base.SetExitStatus + base.Exit with atExitFuncs); runtime code uses throw() for invariant violations and fatal() for startup failures — do not mix.

GOPATH/GOROOT hygiene: go command fatals on GOPATH entries starting with '~' or relative paths and warns when GOPATH==GOROOT; tests run with GOPATH=/nonexist-gopath so code must not depend on a real GOPATH.
The -C flag must be first on the command line and is stripped by handleChdirFlag before dispatch; toolchain re-exec relies on this — new pre-dispatch logic must not break the ordering.

Vendored deps: std module vendors golang.org/x/{crypto,net,sys,text} under src/vendor; cmd module has its own vendor tree incl. x/tools and x/mod — update via normal module workflow then re-vendor; go.mod 'go 1.28' means only language features ≤1.28 are usable.
Contributions go through Gerrit (codereview.cfg), not GitHub PRs; security issues go to security@golang.org per CONTRIBUTING.md; 'go bug' is the recommended issue-filing path.
internal/ packages are import-restricted by the compiler itself (enforced in load/internal), so new shared helpers for cmd tools belong under src/cmd/internal; std internals under src/internal.

report.agent_prompt:
You are working in a clone of golang/go — the Go toolchain source itself (module 'std' for src/, module 'cmd' for src/cmd/), currently at Go 1.28 development on branch master.

BUILD & TEST
- Build from source: `cd src && ./make.bash`. Requires a bootstrap Go >= 1.26.0 in $GOROOT_BOOTSTRAP (never equal to $GOROOT). make.bash builds cmd/dist with the bootstrap toolchain, then `dist bootstrap` builds toolchain1 (asm, cgo, compile, link, preprofile) and go_bootstrap, which rebuilds the tree.
- Full validation: `cd src && ./all.bash`. Tests only: `./run.bash` → runs `go tool dist test -rebuild`. Single regression test: `../bin/go test cmd/internal/testdir -run='Test/fixedbugs/bugNNN.go'`. Package tests: `../bin/go test <pkg>` — always use the built ../bin/go, not a system go.
- Useful env: GO_TEST_SHARDS, GO_TEST_TIMEOUT_SCALE, GO_BUILDER_NAME, GOBUILDTIMELOGFILE.

MAP
- src/cmd/go/main.go: command table in init(); every subcommand is a *base.Command (base/base.go). Dispatch: handleChdirFlag → toolchain.Select → lookupCmd → invoke.
- Build engine: src/cmd/go/internal/work/exec.go (Builder.Do, action DAG, sha256 action IDs, cache). Package model: load/pkg.go — PackagePublic is public API, additive-only.
- Modules: modload (build list), modfetch/fetch.go (download→checkMod→sumdb/go.sum→modcache), vcs/vcs.go (git/hg/svn/fossil shell-out, scheme security).
- Compiler: cmd/compile/main.go → archInits → gc.Main (noder→typecheck→inline/devirt→escape→walk→SSA). Pass table: ssacompile/compile.go (~line 414). Linker: cmd/link/internal/ld.
- Runtime: proc.go (G/M/P scheduler; main() → gcenable → doInit → main.main), mgc.go (concurrent mark-sweep).

HARD RULES
- api/go1*.txt are frozen; only api/next/* is editable, and new lines need a '#issue' annotation. New stdlib API also needs doc/next release notes.
- Regenerate, don't hand-edit: flagdefs.go (genflags.go), opGen.go/SSA rewrites, dist writeGeneratedFiles outputs.
- make.bash must not gain code after the bootstrap call — extend cmd/dist instead.
- go command errors: base.Fatalf; runtime invariants: throw()/fatal().
- Vendored deps under src/vendor and src/cmd/vendor; go directive 'go 1.28' caps usable language features.
- Code review is Gerrit-based (codereview.cfg); security reports → security@golang.org.

SAFE FIRST TASKS: add a test/ regression file, a cmd/go script test under testdata/script, or a stdlib package test. DANGER ZONES: scheduler/GC invariants, write-barrier checks, toolchain switching, module/VCS security gates, and anything touching api/ manifests.
